messages:
incident-bot: SEV1 alert: gateway-prod elevated 5xx rate across us-west/us-east/eu. Error rate ~18% over baseline in the last 2m. Paging oncall: @maya :pager:
maya (oncall): ack, I'm on it. pulling logs and traces now. seeing 502/504s from gateway -> ratecap svc
liam: seeing a pattern: lots of 429s hitting clients then cascading 502s at gateway. sample response:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"rate limit exceeded","tenant":"acme-corp"}
```
chun: fyi I pushed a ratecap config change ~3m ago that tightened shared token-bucket burst (small patch). rolling back now while we confirm impact
maya (oncall): ok please queue rollback. temporary mitigation: scale ratecap pods and enable short prefix cache
liam: creating a bypass list for the busiest tenants as stop-gap. caution: bypass may push pressure downstream. command I plan:
```
rbacctl allow --tenant acme-corp --bypass-ratecap --reason "incident mitigation"
```
sre-lead: pause on bypass for all tenants. instead: 1) scale ratecap 2) enable fail-open heuristics for compatible clients 3) shunt heavy tenants to dedicated fallback cluster. safer path
maya (oncall): scaling ratecap now: `kubectl scale deploy/ratecap --replicas=8 -n prod`
ops-bot: rollout started for deployment/ratecap: desired 8 -> current 2/8 -> 5/8 -> 8/8
liam: also enabling a short-lived in-memory prefix cache to cut KV pressure: `cache.prefix_ttl=5s`
chun: rollback of config submitted: `/deploy rollback ratecap-config@prod` (in progress)
maya (oncall): measurables: after scaling and cache tweak error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in the last 60s
customer-success: CS standby. preparing batch template to message affected accounts (acme-corp, beta-inc). ETA ~20m for initial note
maya (oncall): implementing route shunt for top offenders to minimize user impact. command used:
```
redwood route set --tenant acme-corp --policy shunt --target dedicated-fallback
```
oncall-rotations: reminder: handoff to @chun in 30m. summarize mitigation steps in the incident doc before handoff
maya (oncall): concise summary: root cause likely config change that reduced shared burst allowance -> quota enforcement spike (429) -> gateway downstream timeouts/5xx. immediate mitigations: scaled ratecap, enabled short cache, rolled back config, shunted heavy tenants, prepared customer comms
chun: rollback completed. monitoring metrics for stabilization. dropping packet loss and 5xx trending down
sre-lead: opening bridge: https://zoom/bridge/4187654321 added to thread
incident-bot: bridge created and attached to this thread
maya (oncall): taking initial incident owner. postmortem owner: liam (tentative)
liam: dumping request traces and slowlogs to `/tmp/trace-dump-4187654321.log`. grabbing top 100 trace IDs for impacted tenants for root-cause analysis
customer-success: will send initial PSR to affected customers with ETA and remediation steps. recommend proactive rate-limit guidance for internal customers
maya (oncall): follow-ups to create after stabilization: 1) add deploy-time gating for ratecap bucket changes 2) automated canary for bucket changes at 5% traffic 3) stronger validation in ratecap config tests 4) improve alerts to differentiate config-caused vs traffic-caused spikes
chun: filed a Jira: RED-INC-4187 "Improve ratecap test harness and canary deployments" and assigned to eng-ml + eng-runtime
maya (oncall): switching to monitoring mode. paging remains active until we observe 2 consecutive 5m windows <1% 5xx
sre-lead: noted. thanks all. good rapid coordination. please add any customer-impact notes to the incident doc and mark follow-ups
maya (oncall): incident moving to mitigation->monitoring. thanks team :heart:
